coverageDimensions: SERVICE coverage would mean: which AWS services Audit Manager collects evidence from, or which services each framework's controls assess. This page gives nothing. Not one AWS service is named as an evidence source or assessment target; the seven AWS-named list entries (AWS Control Tower Guardrails, AWS License Manager, AWS Generative AI Best Practices Framework v2, and so on) are framework names, not services in scope, and a parser that harvests them as service coverage is fabricating. REGION coverage would mean: in which Regions Audit Manager is available, or in which Regions a given framework can be used. This page gives nothing — the word Region never appears, there is no Region table, no Region column, no "available in all Regions except" sentence. RESOURCE TYPE coverage would mean: which resource types the controls inspect or which types evidence is collected for. This page gives nothing — no resource type is named anywhere. The only dimension this page supplies is a fourth one: compliance-framework coverage, 29 named frameworks. Take that and nothing else from here; service, Region and resource-type coverage for Audit Manager must come from other pages.

features.featureName: Supported frameworks in AWS Audit Manager (prebuilt standard frameworks in the framework library)
features.reasoning: The page documents exactly one capability: which compliance frameworks Audit Manager ships prebuilt. The values are named external standards and versions — ACSC Essential Eight, ACSC ISM 02 March 2023, CCCS Medium Cloud Control, CIS AWS Benchmark v1.2.0 / v1.3.0 / v1.4.0, CIS Controls v7.1 IG1, CIS Critical Security Controls v8.0 IG1, FedRAMP Security Baseline Controls r4, GDPR 2016, Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act, Title 21 CFR Part 11, EU GMP Annex 11 v1, HIPAA Security Rule Feb 2003, HIPAA Omnibus Final Rule, ISO/IEC 27001:2013 Annex A, NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5, NIST Cybersecurity Framework v1.1, NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2, PCI DSS V3.2.1, PCI DSS V4.0, SSAE-18 SOC 2 — plus seven AWS-authored entries (Sample Framework, Control Tower Guardrails, Generative AI Best Practices Framework v2, License Manager, Foundational Security Best Practices, Operational Best Practices, Well Architected Framework WAF v10). The axis is external because HIPAA, PCI DSS, ISO 27001 and NIST exist whether or not Audit Manager does; the denominator is the world of compliance standards, Audit Manager holds a subset of it, and the same axis is shared with Security Hub standards and Config conformance packs, which makes a ratio meaningful. The catalogue test fails for the axis as a whole — Audit Manager does not define what HIPAA is — but it does apply to the seven AWS-authored entries, which are Audit Manager's own publications and 100% held by construction; flag those so they never inflate an external-standard ratio. Each version is its own value: PCI DSS V3.2.1 and V4.0 are two, the three CIS AWS Benchmark versions are three, the two HIPAA rules are two. Count 29 taken by hand from the 29 bullets of the Topics block and verified line by line.
features.statuses: All 29 are stated as supported/available — the H1 says "Supported frameworks" and the lead-in says "the following list provides an overview of the available frameworks". Zero are stated as not supported: no Yes/No column, no footnote, no "retired" or "deprecated" heading, no negative sentence about any individual framework. Two qualifications must be recorded rather than discarded. First, the Note states the AWS Audit Manager Sample Framework "doesn't support any specific compliance standard" — it is present in the library but maps to no external standard, so on an external axis it is a supported library entry and a non-value: 29 library entries, 28 that name a real standard or published best-practice body. Second, the banner states the whole service "is no longer open to new customers" — a service-level availability fact, not a per-framework exclusion, and it must not be converted into 29 not-supported claims.

pageTitle: Supported frameworks in AWS Audit Manager
shouldNotExtract: The "See also" section and its bullet about skills for AI coding assistants, the Agent Toolkit for AWS, and the aws agent-toolkit search-skills command — AWS boilerplate now appended to every page, never coverage. The availability banner and its link to the availability-change page: a service-level status statement, not a per-framework claim. The introductory paragraph's illustrative mention of "HIPAA, PCI DSS, SOC 2, or more" — prose examples, not the enumeration, and re-extracting them double-counts entries already in the list. The Note's onboarding advice about starting with the Sample Framework — guidance, not coverage. The .md link targets (essential-eight.md, CIS-1-2.md, GxP.md, Sample.md): filenames are not values; the link text is the value. The anchor tag. No quotas, pricing, code examples or troubleshooting appear on this page.
trap: The blanket rule "never extract Topics blocks" destroys this page. On most AWS doc pages the Topics block is navigation; here it is the entire enumeration, and the prose immediately above it says so: "The following list provides an overview of the available frameworks." A parser that drops it returns zero coverage for a page whose only job is to enumerate. The mirror-image trap is worse at scale: switching to "always harvest Topics blocks" turns every other page's child-page menu into fake coverage. The correct rule is conditional — take a Topics block only when the page's own prose designates it as the list of supported things. Secondary traps: collapsing versioned duplicates (three CIS AWS Benchmark versions into one "CIS", two PCI DSS into one, two HIPAA into one) and reporting 25 or 26 instead of 29; reading the H1 word "Supported" as implying a matching not-supported set and inventing negative claims where the page states none; converting the "no longer open to new customers" banner into 29 unsupported or retired entries, when no framework here is marked retired or deprecated; and counting the AWS Audit Manager Sample Framework as compliance-standard coverage after the page explicitly says it "doesn't support any specific compliance standard".
whatThePageStates: This is the index page for Audit Manager's framework library. It says Audit Manager ships "pre-built standard frameworks" based on AWS best practices for compliance standards and regulations, and that "the following list provides an overview of the available frameworks". The enumeration is the Topics block: 29 named frameworks, each linking to its own overview page. The page carries a service-level banner stating AWS Audit Manager is no longer open to new customers, and a Note singling out the AWS Audit Manager Sample Framework as a learning framework that "doesn't support any specific compliance standard". There is no table, no Yes/No column, no Region data, and no service or resource-type data anywhere on the page.
